answers.text: Tell it to always give back the same three lines, same order: date, item and quantity, then any change. The date line is just the date, the item line is item plus quantity, the third is the change or 'no change'.
Ask for one line per claim — date, amount, category, submitter — with a total at the bottom. The total should be all the listed amounts added together for the week.
The dates in this don't quite line up. It calls the 19th three days out, but the call was on the 14th — that's five days, not three.
62 up from 54 does come close to 15%, that checks out. 3 late out of 62 is nearer 95% on-time, not 97%.
I'd sign off Output 2 — it shows its working. You can't see the sales or returns totals behind Output 1's number.
Reply 2's the one I'd send as-is, it names the order and the credit. There's nothing behind Reply 1's claim that it was all our fault.

1. No, better not.
2. Yes.
3. No, not that one.
4. Yes, that one's fine.
5. No.
The pricing and volume discounts I wouldn't paste as-is, that's the sensitive part. That clause naming both parties by name makes me want to leave it out as well.
I'd add a step where someone checks the totals against the system before it goes out. It happens just before the report is sent up, not at some point earlier.
Step 1, where it reads the order and pulls the items, is where a mistake would start. Step 4 is the one that needs a gate, since that's when the email sends with no one looking.
